These frameworks rely on statistical models like Gaussian Processes or tree-based methods to evaluate the performance of various settings. However, such models struggle with settings that affect different parts of a program's execution, as they create correlations that don't align with the typical hierarchical structures these models exploit. To address this limitation, we propose a modified Structured Bayesian Optimization approach, where we adapt the Prior to account for program-specific properties and settings by projecting them onto a common latent space. This approach enables efficient learning of the relationships between settings and performance, as well as facilitates transfer of this knowledge to similar programs. Our method outperforms other optimization techniques in terms of finding high-performance settings with fewer trials, and also demonstrates its ability to handle diverse configuration spaces and learn from related programs.

Our research examined the connection between initial anisotropic geometry and anisotropic flow within a multiphase transport model, specifically for 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions. Contrary to elliptical flow's dependence on centrality, we discovered minimal variation in triangular flow centrality. However, once the influence of initial geometry was removed, vN$^\mathrm{2}$ and vPb2200 GeV Au+Au collisions exhibited an increase in triangular flow at higher nucleon collision multiplicities, also seen in p+Pb and Pb+p collisions. Furthermore, vN2000 and vPb2.76 TeV p+Pb collisions showed v3's relationship with transverse momentum is influenced by centrality and multiplicity, also present in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions.

Over the years, the availability of Linked Data has grown exponentially with more than 10,000 online datasets contributing to the Linked Open Data Cloud.  While many of these datasets adhere to Linked Data principles, they frequently suffer from data quality issues, posing significant challenges for publishers, consumers, and creators of such data.  Although linked quality metadata can enhance the usability of low-quality data, the process of generating such metadata is often time-consuming and labor-intensive.  In contrast, our research introduces an automated, learning-based framework that produces accurate quality estimates for individual data elements, regardless of how many linked quality references are available.  This method leverages existing linked quality metadata, leveraging statistical patterns to provide precise estimations for seemingly unrelated data elements.  Unlike previous approaches, our method is rooted in semantic web practices, ensuring that quality assessments remain tied to their respective data sources and adhering to the decentralized nature of linked data. As such, our technique can be applied to any linked data domain, with demonstrated applications such as Linked Football and DBPedia. Final evaluation results show that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, with comparable results to closely related non-linked data processing techniques.  Moreover, our approach can be applied to previously unreliable datasets such as Music Ontology and GeoNames, with demonstrated performance gains of up to 40 percent in terms of overall accuracy.

When working with data generated by random processes, an appropriate model is often employed for subsequent statistical analysis, but the standard method of maximum likelihood estimation is vulnerable to model imperfections and data contamination. As alternative methods from robust statistics are largely restricted to simple cases, a new approach is proposed as follows - when the true stochastic nature of data is taken into consideration, robust density estimation can be defined and solved via optimization, making it feasible to develop and train robust models for stochastic processes.

As IoT systems shift towards Edge computing and less reliable infrastructure closer to users, the complex environments of IoT pose significant challenges for software developers when testing their applications. Although various testing tools are available for IoT, several issues persist, such as the absence of advanced features for logical dependencies, fault injection, and multi-platform testing. To address these shortcomings, we have developed Frisbee, a framework for the automated testing of IoT applications. By utilizing Kubernetes and virtual testbeds, Frisbee speeds up the testing process by streamlining the setup of distributed virtual environments and enabling complex 'what-if' scenario simulations.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing evaluations of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and the determination of CP-violating processes in $B^0_s \to J/\psi\phi$.

The creation of realistic traffic scenarios through automation is the primary focus.
Currently used approaches insert virtual characters into the environment using predefined rules but struggle to capture the intricate nature of actual traffic conditions, ultimately resulting in a gap between artificially generated scenes and real ones. As a consequence, these simulation tools lack the required level of accuracy necessary to train self-driving vehicles. To mitigate this limitation, we propose SceneGen, a traffic scenario model that utilizes deep generative models (variational auto-encoders) and neural traffic scenario predictions. SceneGen focuses on condensing traffic scenarios into essential elements and reassembles them to improve efficiency. SceneGen significantly enhances realism by learning to predict these elements accurately. Experimental results validate SceneGen's efficacy, showcasing a 50% performance improvement over existing methods on multiple assessment metrics. Furthermore, SceneGen exhibits a substantial improvement in realism when evaluated by human reviewers.
On a Cayley tree, we analyze the Ising model and find novel periodic measures that are linked to index-2 normal subgroups within its group representation.

A critical aspect in designing numerical methods for time-dependent partial differential equations involves identifying the maximum time step size that ensures stability for a given spatial discretization. Research into the regularity requirements that determine this stability parameter has a significant impact on the applicability of a particular scheme. For instance, certain implicit-explicit time discretization techniques are commonly used in practice despite their reliance on highly regularized data due to lack of information on restrictive data regularity assumptions. This paper introduces novel methods to minimize these restrictions and overcomes this limitation by making improvements to the underlying error estimation used in a general framework for constructing convergent iQMR-based methods. The revised approach allows for more lenient data regularity requirements by linking this method's framework to the classic analysis for fully-space methods. By proving novel error estimates for these methods, we have established conditions that ensure stability and accuracy for a particular class of these methods. This is achieved by addressing energy and norm equations, thus providing a more precise understanding of the method's robustness.

A group of integer sequences can be classified as jointly ergodic if for every ergodic system with a measure-preserving nature, their average value converges to the product of individual function values. Jachowski recently made a notable discovery by identifying specific two-sequence patterns, such as (n, An + B), that are not ergodic when shared in common. This research further expands on that finding by exploring additional pairs of sequences (an(d_n)_) that lack the ergodic property, including some involving the Legendre symbol and other mathematical functions. Notably, some of sequences involved in an(d_n) include functions that exhibit ergodic behavior when used separately.

We developed a comprehensive three-phase model for superbubble (SB) growth in low-metallicity galactic environments. These environments allow for efficient radiative cooling of plasma within the SB, leading to its collapse and formation of a dense giant molecular cloud. Using the lephre code, we traced superwind superbubbles' early development in sub-physics-based simulations that accounted for processes like dust destruction, ionized cavities, and grain growth. We found that shock velocities from supernovae typically exceeded the dust destruction threshold, resulting in decreased dust grain sizes within most superbubbles. Dust destruction rates were found to be most significant (around 10^-10 s^-1) near the inner edges of superbubbles, whereas they were minimal (around 10^-12 s^-1) far from the shock fronts. We observed a decrease in destruction rates (around 10^-11 s^-1) for phase II superbubbles that contained dense gas within their walls. We also found that gas within these wall regions experienced significant dust growth rates (around 10^-9 s^-1) and that ionized cavities had dust growth rates around 10^-11 s^-1. These findings have implications for interpreting observations of ionized cavities and dense gas in superbubbles, as well as the relationship between their dust properties and the location of the mass ejection source.

Detecting three-dimensional objects at great distances, or far-field detection, is a crucial capability for autonomous vehicles operating at highway speeds. These vehicles need to be able to spot slow-moving vehicles in the distance that will enter their path in a few seconds. While initial attempts to classify distant objects using support vector machines and global feature methods showed some success, they often require significant amounts of memory and have limited object detection ranges. Although more advanced deep learning techniques have shown great potential, they are not as efficient in terms of memory usage. To address this challenge, we have developed a more lightweight approach utilizing a region-based network with minimal memory requirements. By employing a bounding box refinement method, we have been able to improve classification accuracy in the far-field. Additionally, to overcome the lack of available data for far-field object detection, we have created a new dataset with nearly 200,000 distant regions, and by applying an data augmentation technique using the near-field dataset, we have been able to achieve 95% memory efficiency and 97.5 meters far-field detection range with improved far-field detection performance of 9.31 mIoU.

Chemical reactions are comprehensively understood by exploring potential energy surfaces, which can be visualized as multidimensional landscapes. These energy surfaces often contain local minima, known as reaction wells, that are crucial in determining a system's equilibrium behavior. To accurately predict these equilibrium properties, our group has developed the Tree Approximation Method, initially described in the attached paper. This new approach is an extension of the Tree Propagator Method, which approximates a system's time-dependent Schrödinger equation. As such, the Tree Approximation Method provides a calculable framework for calculating reaction well properties, such as binding energies and zero-point energies. In the context of the Sun-Earth system, reaction well attributes are negligible; however, for triatomic molecules, these energies significantly influence equilibrium configurations. We demonstrate how the Tree Approximation Method can be utilized to compute binding energies and zero-point energies, specifically through an illustration involving water (H2O).

Soft-tissue navigation is highly dependent on non-rigid registration. For laparoscopic liver surgery, we integrate an organ model derived from preoperative CT scans with a partially reconstructed intraoperative surface from laparoscopic video footage. The complexity of this task is heightened by noisy and incomplete data, unpredictable tool-tissue interactions, and insufficient real-time intraoperative sensing. The goal of this study is to enhance the accuracy of real-time non-rigid registration. We achieved this by training a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict the registration deformation field, leveraging both noisy/incomplete surface data and CT scans. The algorithm optimizes the deformation field to align the surface with the laparoscopic images while minimizing the difference between pre and intraoperative organ representations. A key aspect of the algorithm is that the deformation field preserves topological features and maintains a smooth gradient. We validated the approach using synthetic data and evaluated its performance against traditional registration techniques, demonstrating a significant improvement in accuracy.

For a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, research has focused on conformal matter collineations within the energy-momentum tensor. The overall structure of these collineations is determined under non-degenerate conditions, with fifteen distinct, independent forms found. However, when the energy-momentum tensor becomes degenerate, the associated conformal collineations exhibit infinite degrees of freedom. Moreover, specific degenerate subcases may still harbor non-degenerate Ricci inheritance collineations.

Determining scene flow involves calculating the three-dimensional motion trajectories of points within a dynamic environment, and accurately predicting this information is essential for applications like occupant protection in automotive design and flight safety for unmanned aerial vehicles. Recent methods have enhanced our understanding of simultaneous motion and depth estimation, but these approaches rely heavily on preprocessing to track object identities, incurring additional computational costs. An alternative solution is the use of re-identification features, which can serve multiple purposes including change detection in dynamic scenes and real-time activity monitoring in surveillance applications. We introduce an end-to-end trainable network that directly estimates scene flow using Re-Id features, employing a single network architecture comprising an encoder-decoder structure for depth and motion estimation, along with residual connection modules to improve feature learning. Experimental results demonstrate our method's superior performance on benchmark datasets, and further applications of our re-identification module show potential in activity recognition and video surveillance.

In recent years, AI networks, specifically those based on artificial neural systems, have significantly outperformed competitors in various tasks, including image recognition. However, the widespread use of such models is hindered by their dependence on powerful computing power, primarily GPUs, for operational efficiency. In contrast, neural networks can leverage retinal architecture, specifically SPNNs, to enhance computational performance and reduce the need for powerful processing units. We present a Spiking Neural Network model, bio-inspired and designed to predict the location of the frog image within a scene, utilizing a SPNN that translates temporal signals, or events, into precise coordinates. This model demonstrates an 8-fold speed increase in inference, a 4-fold decrease in memory usage, and training times that are 2 to 3 times faster than the deep learning baseline, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of the MIT bag model and a strong magnetic field, subsequently examining the impact of the MIT bag parameter and the magnetic field on the spac diagram of spin-polarized strange quark matter.

A Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property in a graph means that every perfect matching can be converted into a Hamiltonian cycle through local transformations, specifically the 2-factor switching operation. This property has been previously exhibited in cyclically n-fold folded graphs $Z_n^k$ for specific instances. In this analysis, we determine the exact conditions under which the graph $Z_n^k$ possesses this PMH-property.

Recent discoveries in graph theory, specifically in the area of cluster complexes, reveal an interesting connection to the Bunyakovsky Conjecture. This conjecture seeks to identify the conditions under which a quadratic polynomial, taking integer values, will generate prime numbers.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call
filtering policies in containerized applications. During operation, Timeloops
automatically accepts or rejects system calls from applications, enforcing a set of
security rules set. Among other options, Timeloops can effectively replace static
analysis methods that determine system call filtering from a program's source code.
Designed for microservices applications communicating via a message brokering
system like RabbitMQ, Timeloops can operate with minimal performance overhead
and manage the system call filtering of multiple services simultaneously, despite
running on separate machines. We demonstrate that Timeloops can efficiently
enforce system call filtering policies in real-world scenarios, often outperforming
the expected results from static program analysis methods that do not account for a
program's execution context.

To explain the minimal mass of observed neutrinos within the Standard Model framework, theory necessitates an extension that includes right-handed neutrinos. These additional particles can generate small neutrino masses through interactions, potentially leading to observable consequences. Notably, in certain models with multiple Higgs doublets, the presence of multiple Higgs fields can lead to an anomalous decay of the heaviest Higgs boson, especially when right-handed neutrino masses fall within a specific mass range. In this study, we expand upon the Standard Model by adding three Higgs doublets and three right-handed neutrinos, utilizing a discrete symmetry to prevent problematic effective operators. We investigate a scenario where two Higgs doublets possess large vacuum expectation values, leading to anomalous decays of the heaviest Higgs boson. This scenario is consistent with existing experimental data, and we present our findings through parameter space analysis and decay rate calculations for the Higgs boson.

This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target appearance probabilities are organized on a grid. A streamlined variation of the Rao-Blackwellized point mass filter assumes grid cells contain fixed targets or not, eliminating the need for individual cell tracking. Instead, a set of parameters describing the distribution of targets within each cell is estimated through the application of Rao-Blackwellization and Gaussian mixture model (GXM) updates. Our method offers enhanced efficiency over conventional GXM filters, producing fewer components, which in turn reduces processing time, especially in scenarios with low target density. Moreover, our approach generates data association hypotheses that are more aligned with the finite multi-hypothesis GXM filter, thereby producing more accurate results.

This study examines the null controllability of a population model that includes an interior degenerate diffusion component. By first establishing a new Carleman estimate for the adjoint system in its entirety, and subsequently deriving a relevant observability inequality, we aim to demonstrate the existence of a localized control action capable of driving the population towards extinction within a finite time frame.

The dynamics of soccer games mean even small moments can greatly impact the outcome, making players, coaches, and analysts highly focused on understanding these moments. Data is available on each team's position, but action sensor data also reveals the intensity of player interactions. Given these factors, determining the best move becomes crucial, and could potentially influence goals. In this study, we build a real-time scoring model that incorporates these elements and is ready for use within a game, having scant less than one second to construct. Machine learning techniques help simplify the complexity, allowing us to recommend the most effective action. Experimental results show our model can be built in under ten seconds, and comparing it to random actions on teams' positions during the game, our model can increase their chances of scoring up to 35 times more. Nonetheless, the model's accuracy is limited by the defense's real-time positioning, which makes teams' goals up to 10 times more. Despite this, the predictive value of action and the model's design open up exciting possibilities for developing automated training systems.Generate the abstract of a paper that is relevant to the following question: 团队在足球比赛中的最优行动如何受其他因素如球的位置、对方球队的位置和比赛时间的影响？

High-resolution subsurface modeling via seismic imaging has the potential to be greatly improved with Full Waveform Inversion (FWI).  However, FWI's non-convex optimization problem makes it susceptible to getting trapped in local minima.  As an alternative, a model update scheme known as Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (WRI) has been proposed that reformulates the FWI objective function in the time-domain.  Although WRI is more efficient and provides high model contrast resolution, its sensitivity to noise and inaccurate first arrival times limits its robustness.  On the other hand shallow image is shown to be an incredibly effective and computationally efficient initialization method for both FWI and WRI due in part to its ability to accurately map event trajectories from the source and receiver coordinates.  As an attempt to make the model update scheme of WRI both precise and reliable we propose to use shallow image as an initializer for WRI to call it S-WRI.  With this new approach we find that the model update from S-WRI has significantly improved accuracy in comparison to WRI by conducting several benchmark tests.  Furthermore we demonstrate that S-WRI has multiple advantages over FWI and WRI when tested with noisy and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) data.  As such this new approach of formulating the model update from WRI has proven to be both high resolution and robust when initialized with shallow image. We've developed an all-optical technique for producing the nonreciprocal behavior of photons using a Kerr resonator. This method involves applying a significant amount of quantum squeezing to the resonator. Either a squeezing resonator drive or self-squeezing caused by strong microwave photon absorption can achieve this. Then, two opposite-polarity optical tones with different amounts of photon absorption can result in breaking of Lorentz reciprocity. We designed and executed an experiment in which microwave photon absorption created a highly squeezed state in a microwave photonic resonator. This allowed two opposite-polarity optical probes to demonstrate break of Lorentz reciprocity.

We have presented the results from the AstroSat analysis of the high-mass X-ray binary X-ray pulsar IGR J19294+1816 during its Type-I outburst in October 2019. Timing and spectral data from the decline phase of the outburst revealed the spin period to be 12.684 seconds, with significant spectral features. A Quasi Periodic Oscillation was observed at a frequency of 0.079 Hz and an RMS amplitude of 14%. Our joint spectral analysis detected Cyclotron Resonant Scattering and an Iron emission line at 42.7 keV and 6.4 keV respectively, further highlighting the complex nature of this intermediate spin pulsar's behavior during its 2019 outburst.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetrical noisy voter model was developed for a regular lattice structure. The model allows one species to colonize nearest-neighbor sites, while another species can settle at any distance but is less successful in doing so. The model includes external noise, which can lead to random species swaps in the lattice. The combination of these factors can result in stable coexistence, but only under specific conditions where the species with longer dispersability has sufficient colonizing ability and may also depend on the intensity of the noise. The model shows that moderate noise can promote coexistence, while very high noise leads to a random species dominating the lattice. The model also displays a sudden transition to an asymmetric state at moderate noise levels with a distinct scaling pattern. The study has real-world implications, particularly in understanding the impact of habitat fragmentation on colonizing and dispersing species.

Ancient sundials served as primary timekeepers before the invention of mechanical clocks, with the classical Islamic civilization utilizing the Sun's daily movement to determine prayer times, often relying on sundials for this purpose. This knowledge eventually spread to Indonesia through Islamic cultural influences. Indonesian sundials developed as a reflection of local advancements in astronomy, technology, art, and architecture, with historical examples often featuring decorative elements that conveyed religious values. This research focuses on sundials crafted between the 19th and 20th centuries, examining their functionality as time-measuring devices and their aesthetic significance through a thorough analysis of thirty-one selected specimens, highlighting their historical and cultural importance.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. This hybrid network allows a central hub to transfer data to those in need and supply power to those who require it. This coexistence also allows D2D transmissions to use the same band as the wireless optical link. This integrated network is designed to maximize overall utility by balancing benefits of data and power transfers against D2D communication throughput. A general optimization problem is formulated to balance these objectives. Building on existing concepts, a surface reflection pattern is developed taking D2D communication into account. An iterative method, utilizing gradient ascent and a modified direction finding technique, is used to solve the optimization problem. Computer simulations demonstrate that the method converges quickly and effectively, outperforming other solutions in terms of computational efficiency and total system performance.

The surge in telework and online learning necessitates the use of personal
electronic devices for extended periods, which can lead to input discomfort. This
project is designed to facilitate two-dimensional LDV measurement at a distance
of up to 20 cm in a horizontal plane using a single-beam LDV system, with the
capability to evaluate sample reactions and identify potential issues related to
input fatigue. By incorporating a laser Doppler vibrometer, optical encoder, and
two-dimensional LDV measurement system, users can assess the frequency
spectra of samples in real-time as they perform tasks, potentially providing
valuable insights for optimizing interface design and user experience.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is subject to debate, particularly regarding their ability to go beyond simple spherical correction and enable multi-modal and high-resolution applications in Transmission Electron Microscopes. We present an innovative EPPP design that overcomes spatial and temporal limitations imposed by spherical correction, enabling multiple imaging modes at high resolution simultaneously. By programming the phase plate to counteract the Spherical Aberration of the TEM while maintaining this level of precision, we can utilize high-order deflection to create a fine donut-shaped electron beam. This beam is suitable for applications in Energy filtered TEM and analytical modes. Moreover, the design enables high-resolution modes by balancing these high-order deflections, resulting in a centered electron beam. This all can happen at the same time, via the Bessel correction, and with only one degree of freedom. The proposed design is technologically feasible and can be implemented as an integrated component in the existing system of the EP-TEM.

The success of data-driven dialogue models heavily relies on their ability to accurately encode user input to generate relevant and effective responses. While it is common to evaluate the generated text for its semantic and syntactic quality, the underlying representation of this encoding is often overlooked, which can hinder the model's performance in anticipating the next utterance. This work argues that merely assessing text generation metrics is insufficient in gauging a model's understanding of human conversation, which led us to introduce encoding evaluation as an essential aspect of dialogue model development. We investigate this issue across multiple settings and consistently demonstrate that certain architectures outperform others in both text generation and encoding tasks. Notably, we find that incorporating explicit memory components, such as attention over previous dialogue history, enhances both aspects of model performance. Our comprehensive analysis provides valuable insights for future research in dialogue model design.

Deep learning methods for LiDAR data analysis have revolutionized 3D place recognition in autonomous vehicles and robotics by improving local re-localization and loop-closure detection rates in complex environments. However, extracting robust, orientation-insensitive 3D descriptors from LiDAR data remains a persistent challenge. To tackle this, this research introduces a novel, range-based, deep learning network called AttDLNet that leverages an attention mechanism to selectively emphasize contextual and inter-feature connections. The proposed network is tested and validated on the KITTI dataset, with experimental results showing its enhanced performance and loop-closure capabilities when incorporating attention layers. Moreover, the study indicates that incorporating this network's attention layers into orientation-alignment and multi-granularity matching approaches significantly enhances 3D place recognition.

Streaming high-resolution video, whether HD or very HD, requires efficient transcoding, and cloud computing provides a scalable solution for processing large numbers of videos. This research analyzes video transcoding performance across various cloud providers and machine types, and develops a predictive model for transcoding cost and time. The study reveals that cloud machine OS and network do not significantly impact CPU-bound tasks but can become a bottleneck during network congestion. A predictive model developed for Amazon EC2 enables accurate estimation of transcoding cost and time, and is applicable to other cloud environments. Furthermore, an optimal cloud machine selection strategy is proposed to minimize streaming costs while meeting quality requirements.

We have derived a semi-analytical formula for the dynamic density-density correlation of massless Dirac electrons in doped graphene, which is applicable at finite temperatures. This finding is key to understanding the thermal screening of interactions among Dirac electrons and we leverage it to calculate the thermal capacity and compressibility of doped graphene. Notably, at very low temperatures, the thermal capacity displays a linear temperature dependence characteristic of normal Fermi liquids, with the coefficient controlled by the velocity of charge carriers in the material.

Continuous speech leads to consistent prosody patterns, yet current speech synthesis models often disregard context. These systems fall short when it comes to producing high-quality paragraphs. To rectify this, we've developed ParaNet, a context-aware synthesis system capable of integrating semantic, acoustic, and paragraph-level information. By embedding this data into an attention mechanism, ParaNet efficiently utilizes a multi-head design and an alignment enhancement module to ensure co-articulation and align semantic features with acoustic ones. Experimental results have demonstrated ParaNet's superiority over other context-aware systems and ordinary synthesis, especially in producing natural prosody and co-articulation, as well as intelligibility. Our source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/cucugwa/ParaNet-.

We provide explicit definitions for the spectral and orbital stability of solitary waves in a model that includes a Klein-Gordon equation and an anharmonic oscillator. We also conduct a comprehensive analysis of the linearized equation's spectrum at the solitary wave state.

Q-ball studies in a single symmetry theory are common, yet the field can be more expansive, allowing for the examination of theories featuring multiple symmetries in a more general context. In this paper, we explore this broader scenario, analyzing both the standard and advanced limits within this theoretical framework and identifying essential conditions for existence in the more complex scenarios. Additionally, we identify a previously unexamined Q-ball state, which we term 'cored', and demonstrate that it could possess stability under specific conditions; a more detailed investigation into its implications will be addressed in a subsequent study.

We investigated a cyclic universe containing holographic dark energy with different infrared cutoffs, examining the impact of these cutoffs on the universe's early epochs and the necessity for its energy to be thoroughly studied. Our analysis revealed that, contrary to some studies, the Hubble radius cutoff doesn't always accurately represent the true Hubble radius during the universe's contraction phase, particularly when the decay of the fundamental Planck scale was considered. The critical density point in this scenario was shifted to an extremely late time, around $10^{-23}$s, and the corresponding Planck temperature was significantly lower than initially thought, making it feasible for the initial Big Bang to occur at such a late time, providing a potential solution to the entropy paradox in the cyclic universe. Based on the density paradox solution, we proposed that the Hubble radius cutoff may offer the initial conditions for the Big Bang through the mechanism of cyclic contraction and expansion.

Gnutzmann and Smilansky previously developed a formula for the bond scattering matrix of a graph using a Hermitian matrix, for which an alternative proof has been devised, employing a method related to the zeta function of a graph. Furthermore, the formula has been broadened to cover regular coverings of graphs, and a novel 'L-function' concept for graphs has been defined, yielding a determinant expression. This has a corresponding outcome where the extended Gnutzmann and Smilansky formula can be represented by the graph's 'L-functions'.

We derive new conclusions regarding the additive Galois module properties of specific wildly ramified finite non-abelian extensions of Q. Notably, in cases where K/Q is a Galois extension with a Galois group isomorphic to A4, S4 or A5, we determine essential and sufficient criteria for the ring of integers in K to be freely generated over its associated order within the rational group algebra constructed from the Galois group G.

In experiments involving particle collisions, identifying neutral long-lived particles typically relies on observing their decay products or the absence of them due to their interaction with detector material. However, there is another approach that does not depend on the particle's decay. This method is suitable for certain decay processes, such as the decay of certain particles into the combination of a meson and two other potential decay products, such as neutrinos or hypothetical particles like axions. If a significant number of these collisions result in the emission of a particle that escapes detection, it could lead to an observable peak in the missing particle rate, providing evidence for the existence of new, previously unknown neutral particles. This theoretical framework is applied to a specific decay process in particle collisions involving the decay of a specific particle into the combination of two other particles, such as an axion-like particle, and a meson. Using initial production data and assuming mass and coupling range values for a hypothetical particle, it is possible to calculate the most likely outcome of this experiment, such as a certain error range for a specific particle decay rate. Conversely, if such a decay process has already been experimentally confirmed, it could be used to establish new constraints on the existence of a specific type of hypothetical particle.

This study provides a detailed examination of the potential inaccuracies in
the output of contextualized language models when analyzing diachronic semantic
shifts in word meanings. We present an enhanced ensemble method that surpasses
common approaches by evaluating the influence of incorporating external
contextual information and incorporating new dimensions into the training data.
Our results demonstrate that most contextualized methods introduce significant
errors when assessing significant semantic changes over time, likely due to a
tendency in these models to prioritize unusual contextual instances.
However, our improved method shows a substantial reduction in errors compared
to the current standard. Additionally, we investigate the causes of this
shortcoming and offer a practical alternative that on average detects around five
more words correctly with each additional data point.

Active galactic nuclei (AGN) containing active black holes at the center can allow for
investigations into the mass and spin of black holes through analyzing their electromagnetic
spectra. We explore this connection using relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) simulations
that account for an accretion disk and a magnetar. We discover that the presence of a magnetar
affects the observed spectrum of the broad-line region (SBLR) and that this impact can be used
to estimate the strength of magnetic fields around the black hole. We propose two main
methods: modeling the additional emission from the magnetar directly, or by leveraging
breaks in the AGN spectrum to indicate changes in how electrons accelerate, thereby providing
estimates of magnetic field strength. These estimates from process-driven models complement
those derived from features in the AGN spectrum. We further discuss how these strategies can
be applied to observational data.

A distinctive feature of neural development is the rhythmic shifting of cell nuclei
between the upper and lower layers of the neuroepithelial tissue as interkinetic nuclear
migration (IKNM) unfolds. In this study, we utilize extended, high-speed two-photon imaging
to track the movement of individual neural cell nuclei in the developing mouse cortex, resulting
in a comprehensive speed map that reveals the precise rate of karyal movement at different
locations. Our analysis uncovered an unexpected inconsistency in the symmetry of IKNM rates:
while the migration towards the lower cortex appears uniform, there is a notable variation in
the migratory speed towards the upper cortex that is linked to the local distance from the upper
ec tor x is. This asymmetry in IKNM end flows may offer new insights into the opposing forces
acting on the neural cell and could potentially provide key information for understanding
cell behavior and response to mechanical stimuli in neural cells.

In various image processing tasks, including video compressed sensing and color image demosaicing, images must be separated from coded measurements that represent their superposition. Real-world code patterns, which are often non-negative, structured, and non-sparse, make this separation from low-rank images challenging. To bridge this gap, our research develops a novel reconstruction model that accounts for these code pattern characteristics. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem aiming to minimize the norms of the images and code pattern, with respect to their projections, while introducing specific measures for total variation and structure characteristics. To efficiently solve this problem, we propose an alternating direction method of Lagrange multipliers, which involves successive steps of sub-optimization. Our numerical results, compared against standard techniques, demonstrate the superiority of our model in preserving image and video structures and codes' non-negative nature.

We've developed a comprehensive hydrodynamic theory that applies to polar active fluids in the presence of randomly distributed inclusions, and our model demonstrates the possibility of overcoming these obstructions to maintain a non-zero overall speed. Contrary to previous assumptions, the dynamics of this specific class of active matter cannot be accurately captured using simplified hydrodynamic models when the spatial environment is two-dimensional up to five-dimensional space; however, we were able to derive precise, dimension-dependent scaling parameters for these dimensions.

Researchers within the same institution often rely on their institutional email for inter-institutional communication, using their domain as an identifier. A exploitable vulnerability has been discovered in this behavior which can be used for widespread email spoofing attacks. We analyzed this weakness through detailed simulations of research institutions' communication patterns, using data from several universities in South Korea. Our results indicated that this exploit could be used to compromise nearly all nodes within these institutions' networks. Furthermore, it was found that the attacker could achieve a high level of trust from recipients, with two of the universities showing inbound trust scores exceeding 0.9. This research also explored additional factors that could impact the efficacy of this attack and the potential for it to be successful.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, we propose a new idea, 
the concept of an "exceptional" van Hove singularity, where a strong 
electron interaction fragments a continuous Fermi surface into disjoint regions. 
We identify this singularity with the merging of two separated Fermi surface 
segments, and demonstrate that it is close to a van Hove singularity, 
reaching it by adjusting a material parameter affecting its dispersion. 
We assert that, in the broader family of cuprate materials, 
the onset of pseudogap is attainable solely through inducing this exceptional 
van Hove singularity. 
The proposed hypothesis can be tested using the recently invented 
resonating level model, and we show that it naturally produces an 
electron interaction Hamiltonian with the desired hypothetical property, 
allowing for the prediction of a specific cuprate material exhibiting this 
exceptional van Hove singularity.

This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, we discuss the performance characteristics of this apparatus.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements are crucial in validating the findings of space-based missions like TESS. Although the TESS data can sometimes suggest the presence of planets due to the influence of the star's movements, ground-based data helps confirm or reject these possibilities by measuring the actual movements of the star. Although the TESS transits can occasionally be contaminated by other phenomena, the majority of the potential planets found by TESS are likely genuine, and the use of the TESS data combined with ground-based observations is expected to yield numerous new discoveries of exoplanets in the coming years. Although the choice of validating methods depends on the characteristics of the potential planet found, the use of ground-based radial velocity surveys is the most effective way to confirm or confirm the presence of low-mass exoplanets.

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities, such as ID card fraud, which necessitates faster and more efficient methods of detecting such acts.  To facilitate quicker detection, a method has been developed that automatically converts ID cards into readable text, along with locating any national security marks present.  This study employs pre-trained Optical Character Recognition technology to accurately convert ID cards into digital text with high precision, and experimental results demonstrate that this method can accurately convert ID cards and detect national security marks present on them.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces varying in intensity or driving forces that changed over time. Calculations of position expectations were carried out for multiple scenarios of mass, angular frequency, and the lambda parameter in both cases. Constant driving led to coherent states, with theoretical predictions closely matched by both simulation approaches. A discrete-time lattice Metropolis algorithm was used to evaluate the imaginary time path integral for these simulations.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly influences the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best measured through light curves as the phase shift accumulates over time in a quadratic manner. For comets, however, measuring their rotation rates is complicated due to their short life spans and rapid rotation period variations induced by the YORP effect. Using astrometric and photometric data, researchers have extracted the global parameters of the comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenkov, which were verified with onboard measurements. For this comet, a new theoretical model has been developed to estimate the global parameters of its shape, surface properties, and rotation rate, which can be used to predict its future motion and rotation rate. For instance, the model indicates that the comet's global rotation rate will slow down significantly over time, which will have a notable effect on its overall motion and rotation state. For example, the comet's global rotation rate will change from 7.9 hours every billion years to nearly 10 hours every billion years, which will have a significant effect on its overall motion and rotation state.
