The proliferation of social media has transformed how information spreads, 
increasing its rate of dissemination but decreasing its depth of discussion. 
This trend is particularly evident when examining topics that provoke the most 
frequent interactions on Twitter, which turn out to be politics-related issues. 
In contrast, users on Twitter tend to rely on short, brief statements when 
engaging in discussions about these issues, avoiding in-depth analysis. 
To understand why this happens, we applied a theory initially developed for human 
learning to the realm of online discussions. Our research revealed that on 
Twitter, it is more beneficial for a user to initiate a new discussion thread 
rather than participate in an existing one, as this strategy maximizes their 
individual engagement. Surprisingly, this theoretical model's predictions 
align with our observed data, indicating that it is economically rational for 
agents to start new discussions on their own, rather than joining ongoing 
discussions and forming communities within the discussion space.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Precise knowledge of a star's properties is crucial for both stellar astrophysics and exoplanetary science. This study utilizes open-source code to create accurate open cluster members and fake exoplanets, allowing researchers to determine the best methods for recovering accurate stellar properties. When analyzing large datasets obtained from wide-field transit surveys, researchers found that open cluster membership alone is insufficient for recovering stellar properties with high accuracy. Furthermore, they found that the current method used by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to filter out data, known as the "5-sigma rule," does not effectively remove enough noise. As a result, they propose refining the data selection process and utilizing all data points when analyzing large datasets. This study also investigates the influence of radial velocity and activity indicators on the detection of exoplanets with the JWST, revealing that even with data filtering, the effect of these factors can still be significant. The results of this study can inform the design of future data analysis pipelines for large datasets obtained from wide-field transit surveys with the JWST.

Confining modes known as LEWs exist at the interface between two specially designed electromagnetic interfaces called metasurfaces. These line waves exhibit unique properties, such as highly tunable characteristics, effective two-dimensional localization, and stable performance. A practical application of LEEWs can occur in open space, utilizing carefully designed unit cells composed of transmission line loops. Analysis and full-wave simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of LEEWs in minimizing their cell components, achieving two-dimensional localization, and verifying their robustness against disturbances. This realization highlights the potential of LEEWs for generating flexible and adaptable electromagnetic fields.

Although a key function in database management, query evaluation classification lacks comprehensive guidelines when dealing with self-joined queries. Our investigation aims to bridge this knowledge gap by examining how self-joins impact the complexity of enumerating database results, building on existing research. By extending two known, query-based enumeration classifications, we propose a unified framework that accounts for self-joins. This framework provides unified criteria for polynomial-time result enumeration. Additionally, our framework provides a more detailed understanding of self-join effects, identifying conditions under which they increase complexity, provide exponential hurdles, or only marginally impact computation. These findings illustrate that polynomial-time enumeration can arise from combining previously disjoint cases, providing a clearer path forward for further exploration.

Multiple formal models can process functions that map infinite strings to other infinite strings, such as transducers and data automata. We define a unified concept of visibility to compare how input details are preserved by these machines. By redefining traditional transducer operations to fit a general framework of visibility-constrained rewriting, we prove a key property: functions performed by transducers are fundamentally reparable if they are already well-defined, with this repairability holding true even when using data automata.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decay to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics complex systems. Although effective for simple applications with linear or minimal nonlinearity, previous studies on larger, highly nonlinear systems have required significant amounts of data for training. We have developed an advanced version of reservoir computing and demonstrated its capability to track real-world systems with minimal training data. Using a logistic map and a Henon map as examples, our computation shows that this new method achieves superior accuracy with significantly fewer data points. Even when compared to substantial amounts of traditional reservoir computing data, our approach exhibits similar accuracy for simple systems.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involved verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears to maintain effectiveness in high-dimensional settings, as evidenced by simulation results.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers under constraints and worst-case disturbances in variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs formulations, we've developed a second-order successive sweep algorithm for calculating the reachable state space. This approach, which assumes a continuous and smooth Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, enables us to determine the states that can be reached within a given time frame under worst-case conditions and state feedback control.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) have excelled in learning low-dimensional structures within data, finding广泛应用 in various tasks such as signal encoding, cyclical pattern generation, and Gaussian process creation. Despite their success, current implementations typically dedicate separate networks to each spatial dimension or frequency dimension, either separately or in combination, without considering a unified, shared representation that encompasses all dimensions simultaneously. We propose an innovative unified neural encoding framework, utilizing a dual MLP structure with distinct connections across spatial and frequency domains, leveraging their combined capability to model dependencies within images and videos. This method simplifies the network by reducing it to two compact modules, each with approximately 1000 parameters for an image, facilitating efficient inference. We further enhance this model with a unified learning strategy, enabling it to encode multiple videos with diverse characteristics using a single network, removing the need for separate networks or fine-tuning. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate superior performance in compression, learning, and generation tasks, significantly outperforming the current state-of-the-art methods, particularly in terms of accuracy, with minimal performance gaps (around 0.2 dB) in compression and learning tasks, compared to a 2 dB benefit in generation tasks, with all results measured on the DUCO benchmark.

The underlying mechanisms of the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization remain controversial, suggesting that a continuum exists that spans from living to non-living entities. Recent discoveries suggest that this continuum may be governed by distinct factors such as associated motion or conceptual categorization. To better understand the phenomenon, we developed a comprehensive framework that views animacy as a continuum influenced by multiple, overlapping dimensions. Using rigorous statistical analysis, we found that motion and category independently contribute to this continuum, also revealing the existence of an additional factor that we named the "exception factor." Moreover, our research revealed two key hypotheses proposing separate continuums may coexist due to the distinct nature of some neurons that respond equally well to both motion and category. To test these ideas, we conducted rigorous analyses using independent datasets, ultimately providing the field with a nuanced framework that acknowledges the complexity of multiple continuums.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of pre-/postconditions that reflect the relationship between programs' inputs and outputs when comparing pairs of programs.

The rapid transmission of contagious diseases can be significantly driven by a single individual with multiple transmissions, known as a super-spreader event. If such events occur frequently within a community, how do they impact key epidemiological indicators, including those measured through contact tracing networks? We utilize a mathematical model to analyze this, showing that a high-frequency epicentre with intense transmission can be represented by a time-varying initial condition in a standard epidemic model. This approach enables us to solve for a specific case during the early stages of COVID-19 in Milwaukee, where we find that super-spreader events increase transmission by up to 50%. Conversely, their overall influence can be minimal, highlighting the necessity of examining all factors, as indicated by a superSPR model. This finding suggests that the apparent $R_0$ value can vary greatly and may not accurately reflect a community-wide, long-term trend.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in the measurement of the perpendicular component (Bperp). It is shown that the vector inversion method's assumption of uniform Bperp across the analyzed area is a significant contributor to this bias. Furthermore, the effect of spatial variability in Inverse Fill Factor (Binv) and vector instrument polarization sensitivity (epsiv) are considered. Simulations utilizing real instrument data indicate that the bias can reach up to 200 Gauss or more, with larger bias values corresponding to higher Binv and epsiv variability. It is emphasized that accurate vector magnetic field measurements require the calibration of both the Inverse Fill Factor and polarization sensitivity correction factors for each active area sensor element.

A comprehensive analysis has been performed to measure the properties of a young star cluster within the Large Magellanic Cloud, specifically IC2648. Using various techniques, we determined its distance, effective radius, and stellar population, and through photometric data, we also calculated its gravitational influence, gravitational potential, and gravitational binding energy. A selection of 26 similar young star clusters in the LMC were also analyzed to identify patterns. A positive correlation was observed between cluster effective radius and mass, and a negative correlation between specific binding energy and mass and radius, mirroring the behavior of globular clusters. The mass-radius relationship of the LMC young - globular cluster system exhibits similar slopes but distinct intercepts, and cluster velocities of dispersion are more heavily influenced by the galactic gravitational field than by the cluster's own gravity. A study of T Tauri stars within the LMC shows that a cluster is only capable of containing them when its mass surpasses a certain threshold, which for IC2648 is estimated at around 3×10^5 M_⊙.

We present a novel, direct method for calculating the decay width of hadrons
decaying to two photons, often requiring an indirect estimation via off-shell
form factors. The new method offers an uncomplicated way to study volume effects.
In an example calculation, we apply this approach to $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$.
Using lattice ensembles with three $N_f=2$ configurations at different lattice
spacings, we derive the final decay width $\Gamma_{\eta_c\gamma\gamma}=6.57(15)_{\textrm{stat}}(8)_{\textrm{syst}}$ keV,
considering systematics such as continuum extrapolation, charm quark mass
renormalization, and electromagnetic mass shifts. Our technique and results can
be extended to additional processes.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces an additional computational cost associated with the Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, which poses a significant barrier for large-scale simulations. Our proposed architecture, based on a novel application of complex-valued affine coupling layers in neural networks, efficiently circumvents this challenge by achieving linear scaling of the determinant cost. As a result, this method allows us to explore the system in the entire complex plane without incurring an unmanageable computational expense.

This paper examines the relationship between integers that are y-friable (or y-smooth) and the Dickman function. By building on the work of Saias, we establish a new result: for any positive constant $C$, there exist constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ depending only on $C$ such that for sufficiently large $y$, the absolute difference between $\Psi(x,y)/x$ and the sum of $\rho(t)x^{-t}$ for $2\le t\le \log x/\log y$ times $y^{\omega(y)}/y$ is less than $x^{-\log y/\log \log y - c_1\log \log y]$ for all $x$ in the interval $[y, x_2(y)]$, where $x_1(y)$ and $x_2(y)$ both grow faster than any power of $y$ (specifically, $x_1(y) = \exp(y^{C})$ and $x_2(y) = \exp(y^{1/o(1)})$). This result on the error term associated with the count of y-friable integers extends a similar finding by Saias regarding the error term for the smooth function.

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling at most C, in the sufficiently large integers n in N. If σ is recognizable and letter-to-letter, then p_Y and p_X grow at similar rates, whereas if σ isn't letter-to-letter, there are instances where p_X isn't proportional to p_Y. As a result, topological entropy h_X isn't necessarily preserved when applying σ to X, indicating that defining topological entropy for free group currents F_N isn't feasible. Nevertheless, we can distinguish currents with or without zero or positive topological entropy.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which employs unlabeled samples to selectively draw from existing data, fine-tune the model for better performance.
Our experiments demonstrate that a carefully chosen loss function and the strategic inclusion of unlabeled samples ReCross can significantly outperform other methods, particularly in challenging generation tasks.
Furthermore, our results suggest that retrieval augmentation is a effective way to mitigate the common issue of catastrophic forgetting during the model fine-tuning process.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh Kernel ('m-ar-K') Fast Independent Component Analysis ('FastICA') approach ('m-ar-K-FastICA') for feature extraction, combining kernel-based dimensionality reduction with ICA to capture both linear and non-linear relationships in data. While previous studies explored the kernel arc-sine (‘ar-K’) FastICA ('ar-K-FastICA') method, which demonstrated success in initial experiments, it suffered from convergence issues in complex scenarios. The proposed 'm-ar-K-FastICA' algorithm overcomes these limitations by introducing the generalized arcsinh (‘m-ar-sh') function, which allows flexible adjustment of parameters to suit various types of data. By comparing 'm-ar-K-FastICA' with its 'FastICA', 'ar-K-FastICA', 'm-ar-SyncICA', and 'm-ar-Square-Root-FastICA' counterparts, results show that it consistently outperforms these alternatives, especially in handling complex random data. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits enhanced stability and convergence properties, attributed to the beneficial characteristics of the 'm-ar-sh' function, including its derivative properties that facilitate the stabilization of optimization processes.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space is, therefore, crucial. In this paper, a generalized framework is established to determine an optimal balance between privacy and performance, and three cost-effective algorithms are systematically examined within this framework: evolutionary optimization, Bayesian methods, and reinforcement learning. The results of our experiments, conducted using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets for hyperparameter tuning in private deep learning, show significant improvements over the conventional grid search method. The paper addresses existing challenges and potential research directions in the field, and provides an open-source code for hyperparameter tuning in private deep learning.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and proposed an analytical method for characterizing and removing it. Through various simulations, we determined the optimal strategy for NISP, which involves taking two readings per integration period and using cross-correlation to reduce the noise. This approach ensures that the instrument can meet its scientific goals despite the presence of correlated readout noise.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 34,410 stars in the Milky Way disk using a vast dataset from the APOGEE-2. The study involved using a two-component model to break down elemental patterns into supernovae types (prompt and delayed). The model was then used to analyze 16 key elements, with some showing complex variations that cannot be explained by this model. We observed that the complex variations are linked to specific types of supernovae explosions and cannot be ignored in studies of the galaxy's structure and evolution. The model also showed that the occurrences of the prompt and delayed events are not evenly distributed, which has implications for understanding the history of the galaxy.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020 and caused severe consequences in China. Due to the anonymity of the online environment, fake news and rumors proliferated on social media, complicating effective pandemic prevention and control. We examined the Weibo platform and examined the characteristics of users who share rumors, as well as the distribution and temporal evolution of rumor propagation. Our analysis revealed that微博 users who share rumors tend to have higher account ages, that rumor propagation peaked in late February 2020 and was followed by extended tail periods in early to mid-March 2020, and that rumor-sharers exhibit power-law distribution patterns in terms of account age, follower count, and output frequency. These findings may aid in developing targeted rumor prevention strategies.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae, specifically due to their nearly universal brightness pattern. Determining the precise distances to galaxies through planetary nebulae analysis relies on a comprehensive understanding of the nebulae's properties, typically achieved by examining their individual spectra. Unfortunately, this exhaustive method becomes impractical when faced with large datasets containing thousands of nebulae. In this study, a large dataset of planetary nebulae were collected within the nearby galaxies of M31 and M33 using a high-throughput survey utilizing the DESI Legacy Flowpipe survey and DESI. With a total of 1450 nebulae successfully analyzed, a non-standard method of statistical analysis, namely machine learning, was utilized to calculate the distance uncertainties to these galaxies. Through this analysis, a 10% margin of error was established for the measurements of galaxies' distances based on their planetary nebulae spectra. Moreover, this study also demonstrated how the method of machine learning can effectively extract detailed information regarding the distribution of planetary nebulae, specifically their characteristics, and the 'velocity dispersion' of each nebula.

Every day, hospitals around the world collect vast amounts of physiological data from inpatients, often leading to data sets that exceed available storage and require robust analytical methods to identify disease patterns and improve patient care. To address this challenge, we introduce \emph{LifeStream}, a system designed to handle the continuous acquisition, processing, analysis, and storage of physiological data in real-time. Like traditional streaming engines, LifeStream can process and compute patterns in real-time, but with specific optimizations for physiological data, allowing for the creation of complex queries in a high-level language that automatically generates optimized execution plans. These optimizations enable LifeStream to deliver significant performance improvements, up to $4\times$ faster than unoptimized results, and in certain cases, a $10\ttimes$ reduction in memory usage, while maintaining equivalent or improved accuracy to batch analysis methods. Furthermore, LifeStream can process and compute patterns in real-time with negligible differences in accuracy to post-hoc analysis, while using substantially less storage and computation resources.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified for curves in a four-dimensional Euclidean space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that certain, previously underappreciated loss functions, including the KL divergence, can yield superior outcomes compared to established methods, underscoring the need to view loss function choice as a parameter amenable to optimization, rather than a fixed constant.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application design. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach for the total deformation gradient, employing the series product method. This allows for the separation of elastic and viscous deformation gradients, which then enables the derivation of appropriate constitutive equations.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we computationally investigate magnetic susceptibility in nematic and chiral superconducting states using the Ginzburg-Landau formalism near its critical temperature. A key observation in our research is that when Bi$_2$Se$_3$ is in the chiral superconducting phase, it behaves as a type-I superconductor, whereas the type of the superconductor changes to type-II in the nematic superconducting phase. Calculations of magnetic susceptibility also indicate that doping Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with hole carriers results in a substantial enhancement of its superconducting critical field, which is in contrast to the relatively modest increase seen when doping with electron carriers. A potential solution to resolve a contradiction between earlier transport measurements of Bi$_2$Sr$_3$CuO$_5$ and theoretical models of Bi$_2$Se$_3$ is that when Bi$_2$Sr$_3$CuO$_5$ is in its hole-doped, hole-hole separated, and nematic superconducting state, its critical field could be higher than previously estimated.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining perfect optimal demonstrations from a teacher is a challenging task, largely due to the difficulties associated with state-space retrieval. As the state space grows larger, the probability of the teacher providing high-quality optimal feedback decreases. In this research, we present an Policy Imitation Learning (PIL) framework that leverages suboptimal demonstrations to generate optimal states, thereby facilitating more optimal feedback. The core components of this framework include an optimal-state generator, an imitation learning module, and an optimization method to prioritize optimal states over suboptimal ones. The proposed framework has been put to the test in a complex multi-robot navigation task, and the results show a substantial 15% improvement in the final model's performance, alongside enhanced generalization capabilities.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure makes its implementation uncomplicated, involving the product of a received baseband signal and a time-reversed version of one symbol duration. Nevertheless, it experiences reduced signal-to-noise ratio compared to coherent detection methods. In this research, the performance of conventional differential detection is enhanced through increased delay periods. By accounting for $K$ symbol delays, the trellis structure and relevant branch and cumulative metrics are derived, resulting in an optimized criterion for $K$. This criterion is based on the minimum Euclidean distance between differential signals, ultimately facilitating the selection of ideal delay periods for popular CPM formats through simulated error rates verification.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations differ significantly from standard parameterization models, especially in predicting the number of merging black-hole and neutron-star systems. Our research utilizes full 1D hydrodynamic simulations of over 800 low-to-intermediate mass stars to examine current and generated simulations' relativistic gravitational-wave source catalogs. Our results show core-collapse simulations can produce final compact remnants in roughly 90% of cases, but also reveal that models may underestimate certain system counts due to factors like supernova explosions and direct stellar collisions. When using more accurate mass ratios in these comparisons, the predicted system counts increase by about two-fold. In addition, our study derives final masses and spins for compact binaries in catalogs, with the majority of black-hole and neutron-star systems forming within the first billion years after the universe's inception, although a small percentage of relativistic mergers occur later and may be distinguishable from other system types.

A previously reported finding from the research of the 1990s and 2000s is the non-thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems' volume dependence, specifically the variation in fluctuations relative to the mean, which is now examined through the lens of statistical thermodynamics and related to compressibility. Through the application of Quantum Field Theory in real-time formalism, this study re-evaluates the compressibility of the 1+1 dimensional massless Dirac field, finding that it aligns with Field Theoretical results at zero temperature and chemical potential, and demonstrates a $T^2$ dependence at zero chemical potential for non-zero temperature. Furthermore, the positive nature of computed finite-temperature, zero chemical potential quantization is confirmed, indicating the absolute stability of this quantum field, with implications for the stability of charge conjugate dyons in the deconfined phase of Quantum Chromo-Dynamics.

Current deep learning techniques used for removing rain from images have achieved notable success in processing artificially created rainy images.  Nonetheless, their effectiveness significantly decreases when confronted with genuine rainy conditions, primarily because they often employ highly simplified models of rain which contrast with the complex real rain scenarios.  This research proposes a new approach that aims to develop a more complex transformation model for rain that includes multiple layers of overlapping, distorted rain with varying speeds and opacities.  This complex model is key to understanding the intricate relationship between rain and visible light.  To create this complex transformation model, a new data generation method is used which involves a complex optimization process that ensures accurate simulation of light transmission.  This new model is designed to address the degrading effect rain has on images and leads to the development of a new approach that combines this complex transformation model with unsupervised metric learning in an attempt to minimize the complexity of rain.  This new approach is evaluated experimentally and shows a major improvement in handling multiple layers of rain and real rainy conditions, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods in these areas.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-sections of a branch in the model's input, effectively making the most of their input interactions. This input-sensitive batch processing leads to significantly more efficient use of human feedback, resulting in improved model performance with less training time. By incorporating innovative tree structures and decoding methods, we make optimal use of human input, outperforming existing methods in multiple benchmarks and application scenarios, even when human resources are limited.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions for classes of theories, which have been reported in papers by S. Shelah and J. Reitz that became available on the arXiv after the 20^\text{18} decision in set theory. Specifically, the studies reveal a parameterized classification of theories in sets that lack a specified continuum. This classification demonstrates the existence of theory towers for sets with possible smaller and larger continuums. Furthermore, it shows that a certain theory cannot be a model companion for any given continuum. This research has significant implications as a negative result regarding classifying theories by the size of their underlying set of reals, particularly in light of the non-decidable nature of the Con(T) problem for theory T consisting of the axioms of ZFC plus the negation of multiple instances of the G\"odel's first incompleteness theorem.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial, and online surveys have proven effective in gathering relevant data. The data collected includes questions about the individual's knowledge of others who have consumed or abused substances, as well as a range of other factors including their age, gender, education level, and more. The data analysis employs a diverse range of techniques, from basic risk profiles to complex machine learning models. The goal is to identify any connections between a person's personality and their likelihood of drug abuse, based on the data collected, which uses the Big Five personality test to assess each respondent. The analysis includes examining the relationship between the personality traits of each respondent and their opinions on the extent of drug abuse or consumption among people who know them personally or not. The data analysis also makes use of the HMMT framework to ensure a fair comparison of predictive models, particularly in scenarios where the target variable is unknown for each person. The results indicate a clear connection between a person's personality and their opinion on the prevalence of drug abuse among people they know, as well as an exploration of whether this connection can be utilized to predict the personality traits of a new individual based on their response to a single survey question. The data set is also suitable for multiple experiments using the HMMT framework, including examining the connection between a person's personality and their likelihood of drug abuse or consumption, which is the ultimate objective. Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  This atlas of inferential knowledge, structured as conditional relationships (if X, then Y), stands out from other available datasets that are centered on categorization, by providing a framework that accounts for causality and effects, actions versus thoughts, and intentional versus unintentional actions.  We have developed nine categories of these relationships and demonstrated the efficacy of incorporating these patterns into models of artificial intelligence.  Our findings reveal that through generative training on ATOMIC, our models can be evaluated using questions of what-if scenarios and have achieved performance gains of up to 30 percent.  These results also show that incorporating causal relationships significantly boosts the modeling of categorization and other forms of learning.

Portfolio optimization in finance can be significantly improved by incorporating portfolio diversification and portfolio returns predictions, according to research. This approach, however, is typically inefficient. A portfolio management strategy that leverages the HHL algorithm for sparse, high-dimensional, and linearly-constrained integer quadratic programs has been proposed to decrease computation time and associated costs. This strategy's effectiveness in delivering an optimal portfolio with improved efficiency has been demonstrated through a specific investment example and comprehensive performance analysis in comparison to conventional approaches like the coordinate descent method, confirming the HHL's efficacy in achieving accuracy and efficiency.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large amount of unpaired text data through multi-modal training, it's essential to address two challenges: synchronizing the sampling rates of speech and language features and ensuring that the learned representations from the pre-trained text encoder do not hinder the ASR task. This paper presents a new bidirectional attention ASR model that utilizes a multi-granularity text pre-training attention module to minimize these challenges. 

First, we show that combining the previously mentioned challenges results in degraded ASR performance, either with separate or joint consideration. 

Then, we propose a novel model that incorporates pre-trained sub-encoder modules for speech and text features, where we align their sampling rates using the upsampled/downsampled feature structure, and design a bidirectional attention mechanism to exchange the attention results between the cross-modal sub-encoders to ensure the learned representations are beneficial for both the text pre-training and ASR tasks. 

Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms the existing methods on three public datasets. 

Then, we show that our proposed model significantly outperforms the current methods on three public datasets. 

Finally, our proposed attention mechanism outperforms the existing methods in terms of task performance. 

The current results demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms the existing methods and achieves a new state-of-the-art on the ASR task.

This analysis focuses on an extended version of the Gnomon Problem, which is about
optimizing the cross-sectional area of a solid relative to its orientation. To begin with,
the study identifies specific requirements that must be met by the cross section. It also
outlines the local optimization rules for cross-sectional optimization and provides a
general method to find the optimal point arrangement on a given surface shape. In addition,
the arrangement of points that yields the highest average cross-sectional area is proposed for
concave geometric forms like ellipses, triangles, and trapezoids. Furthermore, the
arrangement of points that yields the highest average cross-sectional area is proposed for
convex polygons and ellipses.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, denoted as $\pi_n$. We establish that the first $k_n$ positions of $\pi_n$, $\pi_n(1)$ through $\pi_n(k_n)$, are asymptotically independent and identically distributed with a uniform probability distribution over the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for two different distance metrics. When the number of initial positions $k_n$ grows at a rate slower than $\sqrt{n}$ for the total variation distance and slower than $n$ for the Kolmogorov distance, this asymptotic behavior is shown, thereby extending previous findings by Diaconis and Hicks (2019). Furthermore, this work also derives rate bounds for the convergence to this asymptotic behavior. Our results are based on an analytical approach that involves conditioning on the associated associated cluster graph being connected. This method builds upon earlier work by Berman, Konheim, and Lients (1967) who studied the dynamics of the random uniform parking function through a cyclic shifting procedure.

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, potentially blocking conduction. The critical voltage of these nanowires is observed to be tunable using an adjacent gate electrode and varies significantly in response to applied voltage, aligning with expected results of quantum interference but exhibiting unanticipated periodic variations. The magnitude of these variations far exceeds predictions based on capacitance and resistance in the nanowire, and may be attributed to the influence of an underdamped quantum phase qubit coupled to the nanowire. The observed behavior provides a foundation for developing a novel type of superconducting circuit with both quantum phase qubit and coherent conduction capabilities, controlled by both quantum and classical means.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a complete analysis of its atmosphere has not been performed. We utilized a comprehensive database of line transitions to conduct a detailed analysis, which provided an improved fit to the observed spectrum than previously done. This in turn enabled a more accurate estimation of the object's physical properties. Our results indicate a mass of approximately 0.158 times that of Jupiter and a temperature of 697 K, which aligns closely with GJ 229B's mass estimate derived from its orbital dynamics around its host star, given the system's well-determined distance.

Our investigation into the structure functions $F_2$ and $xF_3$ of the proton in a thermal environment is carried out within the framework of perturbative QCD. Specifically, we apply the JIMWLK and BJLMP formalisms to account for the proton's wavefunction using a color glass condensate description. By applying the light-cone current correlation function and the optical theorem, in conjunction with the jet distribution method, we derive expressions for the functions in the Bjorken and xF physics regimes. For the regime of large $x_F$, we derive an explicit expression that incorporates the proton's twist-4 dynamics. Under certain conditions, the Bjorken scaling observed in deep inelastic scattering is also expected to be restored when the proton interacts with the thermal medium, assuming the virtual photon's interaction point is not influenced by thermal effects. Consequently, our study suggests that Bjorken and $x_F$ scaling can serve as possible signatures for the existence of a quark-gluon plasma.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation that enables efficient novel view prediction. Our approach achieves remarkable results, surpassing state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual fidelity and structural organization, as demonstrated by evaluations and user studies.

In this research, inter-orbital coupling was demonstrated using femtosecond laser writing, which enables orthogonal modes in a photonic lattice to couple with each other at different spatial locations. We characterized an asymmetric double-well structure, mapped its propagation dynamics and successfully created a device capable of spatial mode conversion anywhere within a one-dimensional waveguide array. Contextual variational methods were utilized to efficiently describe the nonlinear behavior of this asymmetric structure.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and has only been marginally detected in past experiments, has primarily been studied using theoretical methods so far. A study aims to explore this particle's properties with a quark model that has linear quark-antiquon potentials. It leverages the quark model's success in predicting light and charmed baryons but struggles with heavier baryons like the Ω-. To address this, a new set of diagonal Yukawa-type four-body potentials are introduced, based on the exchange of gluons, gluballs, mesons, and dibaryons. These potentials have since accurately predicted meson and charmed meson properties. Using a minimal basis of these diagonal interactions, a detailed search for low-lying Ω-baryon resonances has been undertaken with a variational method, yielding results that have been compared to previous predictions and experimental data. The study finds that the total potential for the Ω-baryon is dominated by the meson exchange contribution, allowing for a simplification of the model. Furthermore, a finding of interest is that the dibaryon exchange contribution, although crucial for other baryons like the proton, neutron, and Λ-c-, has little impact on multi-strange and multi-charmed baryon resonance states.

Airborne transmission risk in confined environments like buses is intricately affected by the interplay between turbulent airflow and enclosed surfaces that hinder the movement of aerosol-laden particles. To better understand this complex dynamic, our novel approach combines statistical models of turbulent velocity with Lagrangian simulations for shorter timeframes and Eulerian simulations for longer periods. This hybrid method allows us to examine how different variables, including the type of turbulence and acoustics, impact infection likelihood over extended periods, while also considering human respiratory system vulnerabilities. Our findings shed light on the infection potential of airborne viruses, with our detailed solution offering a more comprehensive model than previously available.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical lasers, considering various possible outcomes. To aid in detecting quantum vacuum effects experimentally, our analysis focuses particularly on situations where x-ray photons show differences not just in polarization, but also in direction of propagation and potential energy changes.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, an idea where an encryption scheme prevents adversaries from producing two encrypted versions of the same message based on copies obtained from a benign source. We enhance this concept with a stronger definition and prove that public-key encryption can achieve it, specifically showing that any standard public-key encryption scheme can be converted into one that is unclonable in a single copy setting. Notably, our reduction does not assume the adversary has access to an encryption oracle.

This study confirms that physical layer-based authentication is achievable in
Gaussian noise environments, with the caveat that an all-knowing adversary cannot
be overcome. An scenario is defined where an legitimate sender and receiver can
be reliably identified with an security guarantee. Both optimal methods for this
scenario are found to be simple and involve basic pre-processing of received
signals, specifically linear equalization and Karhunen-Loève transformation.
Notably, when more than one noise source is present, equalization proves to be
equally effective as Karhunen-Loève transformation in this context.

We utilize the full tight-binding model and a semi-orthogonal method to examine flat bands in (MoSe2)n nanoribbons and BT-MDCs at various angles and coverages. Our study reveals that achieving low-damped, quasi-flat plasmon states in these structures demands precise control over their dimensions and edge characteristics. Specifically, flat bands without charge carriers in the outer layers and with filled inner layers are more stable. Our findings also indicate that plasmon energy levels and flatness are significantly influenced by these factors, with the most pronounced variations occurring in angle-independent TB models. In contrast, real-space TB models demonstrate their robustness against damping and external influences, thus highlighting their potential for practical applications.

This paper expresses the potential function $f$ associated with an almost conformal gradient Ricci soliton on a Sasakian manifold in terms of the scalar field $p$, determining when the potential function is constant, and establishing a link between $f$ and $\lambda$. We also establish a condition for a conformal Ricci soliton to be a gradient Ricci soliton, and provide a characterization of the soliton in terms of its contraction or expansion rate.

Both celestial bodies can experience mass loss due to an expansive outward flow,
often regulated or redirected by magnetic fields that create a surrounding
magnetospheric field. Powerful star winds are generated when the magnetic field
accumulates enough energy to be released in sudden bursts, typically occurring
near the star's surface where the magnetic field intensity increases sharply. In
comparison, wind formation from less massive stars, including our Sun, results from
the accumulation of outflows that over time escape the star's magnetic field.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect involves a rise in Spin-Orbit Coupling near a strong spin-orbit material's interface with an adjacent layer. This phenomenon has been observed in various systems, such as graphene and ferromagnetic layers, and controlling Spin-Orbit Coupling is essential for developing Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Tunnel Junctions and other spintronic devices. In this study, we theoretically analyze the Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect in a Heusler alloy layer adjacent to a heavy metal, specifically focusing on Nitride Heuslers such as $${\mathrm{Lu}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrN}}$$. We found that Nitride Heuslers exhibit very high Spin-Orbit Coupling due to strong Spin-Orbit Coupling in the Ir d-bands, and we used first-principles calculations and a three-band model to determine the Sign-Orbit Proximity Coefficient (SOCPC). This coefficient quantifies the additional SOC in a Nitride Heusler sample induced by the Heavy Metal, and we determined the SOCPC for various combinations of Nitride Heuslers and Heavy Metals. Unlike the SOCPC in epitaxial systems, where the SOCPC equals the difference between the two materials' intrinsic SOC values, we found that the SOCPC in sintered powder samples does not follow this pattern. This paper provides approximate solutions to the time-independent fractional Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalised Mie-type potential. We offer solutions numerically using the Riemann-Liouville fractional derivative and present tabulated results for energy eigenvalues and corresponding eigenfunctions. Our findings are supported by numerical calculations performed in MATLAB.

We analyze how enforcing a neural network's Lipschitz continuity, as it pertains to input sensitivity, affects its performance. In our research, we found that lower Lipschitz constants correlate with reduced accuracy, creating a challenge for balancing generalization and accuracy. We propose an alternative approach that leverages this relationship to improve performance finding we can train a neural network with increased Lipschitz constant to achieve highest accuracy, then prune it to attain original network's performance, thus showing connection between input-suppresseion-based attack defense and network security.

Sequential neural network models are highly effective at learning from text's linear structure, but their inability to handle sentences' inherent hierarchical nature limits their ability to predict agreement in low-agreement languages like Basque. This research explores whether these models can predict agreement in Welsh, a Celtic language with grammatical features similar to Basque. We augment the corpus with English and Dutch texts in our experiments. Our key findings show that prediction performance for Welsh and Dutch exceeds that of Biblical Arabic, a language with extensive morphological agreement. Furthermore, our results align with linguists' and psychologists' observations on the challenges of processing Welsh. Notably, we observe a discrepancy between performance on textual data and listener comprehension, indicating that humans can utilize additional information beyond language knowledge when listening to speech.

HD80606b, a planet with a highly eccentric orbit, experiences a 10-fold increase in the energy it receives from its host star as it moves from one point of its orbit to another. This massive influx of stellar energy causes the planet's atmosphere to heat up significantly, which in turn modifies the way it radiates energy. Our research reveals that the planet's atmosphere may also experience permanent changes due to these events, as they might trigger the destruction of molecules and cause surface materials to vaporize. To fully understand the atmosphere's composition, it's essential to consider both the irreversible changes and the heat fluctuations the planet experiences. Utilizing three-dimensional atmospheric models, we've found that the planet's surface material may completely vaporize at periastron, releasing a massive amount of vaporized rock that will take a significant amount of time to recondense. The presence of this atmospheric vapor will also cause the rate of energy the planet receives to increase by as much as 20%. These findings suggest that highly eccentric planets are highly susceptible to long-term atmospheric changes as they are constantly bombarded by extreme heat.

Effective upper limb rehabilitation is essential following a stroke but often requires repeated, repetitive exercises which can be tedious and reduce motivation. To counter this challenge, therapeutic exercises can be made more engaging through modified video games designed specifically for rehabilitation purposes. Successful implementation of such designs demands continuous feedback from therapists regarding user motivation during training sessions. To gather this input efficiently, we've developed a post-it board interface that real-time researchers can access from their lab, enabling non-tech-savvy therapists to provide motivation feedback effortlessly. Our study involved 10 therapy sessions with 7 individuals who had experienced a stroke, using the upper limb for daily activities. These sessions employed a specific video game design called TUGS, and were followed by the collection of motivation feedback. To analyze and visualize this feedback, we utilized topic models and a force-directed graph, and also solicited user input on the feasibility of our motivation feedback approach.

Our research offers a variational approximation, drawing from the Ambrosio-Tortorelli model, to quantify brittle fracture energies in complex, piecewise-rigid structures, applicable to both nonlinear and linearised elasticity frameworks.

We investigate the possibility of lepton-flavour non-universality in certain processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). To this end, we focus on Drell-Yan ditau production and calculate precise corrections to this process, taking into account the effects of quantum chromodynamics at the next-to-leading order. A specialized code is developed to efficiently generate these corrections, allowing for more accurate simulations of ditau events. By applying these simulations to recent LHC data, we are able to place constraints on a type of exotic particle, known as vector leptoquarks, based on their mass and coupling strength. This code can be applied to other processes, such as ditau plus jets production, and may help improve our understanding of these particles at the LHC.

Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans restricts their use for sensitive groups, such as pregnant women and young individuals requiring frequent imaging, due to compromised image quality from lower doses or shortened scan times. Deep learning methods have shown great potential in enhancing PET images by learning non-linear mappings from low-quality to high-quality images using paired or unpaired pairs of paired data. However, existing approaches either lack the ability to generate highly detailed images or involve significant computational costs for pair-based methods. In contrast, unsupervised techniques struggle to produce high levels of detail. We propose-d a novel domain adversarial network (DAN) model trained in an unsupervised manner to transform low-resolution PET images into high-resolution ones with high detail and speed. Our model employs two innovative designs: a shrinking attention network module that efficiently aggregates contextual information without excessive memory usage, and a lightweight network structure that achieves optimal performance. To evaluate its capability in real-world applications, we trained our model using paired data on healthy volunteers and found it capable of delivering high-quality images with significantly reduced radiation exposure (up to four times) or shorter scan times (up to four times), o r both. Moreover, our model's productivity of enhancing low-dose PET images aligns closely with the theoretical limits set by optimal filtering methods, surpassing conventional image reconstruction algorithms in terms of clarity.

The issue of tailoring news to individuals' interests while respecting their data remains unresolved. Growing worries about over-collected data and its unintended use have motivated our research on balancing personalization and privacy. Our experience creating personalized content platforms that protect users' confidentiality has sparked an investigation into users' attitudes towards these topics. A conducted survey revealed the opinions of various age groups regarding personalization and privacy. In this research, we are sharing our key discoveries with publishers and the community to inform the design and development of next-generation news recommender systems, which should prioritize the human user and achieve a harmonious balance between personalization and privacy.

A linguistic analysis known as centering theory examines how coherence in conversations is established through the use of pronouns and other referential expressions. This study adapts centering theory to a less formal context, examining the coherence of comments posted on YouTube videos. By applying the theory to the comments, a model was developed to identify the 'current center' in the discussion. Furthermore, a custom relevance metric was created to assess the 'direction' of the discourse. The analysis revealed that the progression of the discussion on YouTube tends to follow the expected patterns of successful coherence, as seen in more structured forms of communication.

We have devised three new parameterized algorithms for identifying whether a directed graph can be represented in an upward planar layout. Specifically, we've developed a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the number of source vertices, an XP algorithm based on the graph's treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the treedepth parameter. Our novel method combines parameterized techniques with SPQR tree-decompositions, extending previous tractability findings on series-parallel graphs, single-source graphs, and outerplanar graphs.

The rising intricacy of modern adaptable systems demands elevated automation in their configuration process, thus also accelerating development cycles via rapid, automated workflow integration. A novel automated configuration framework is introduced, using model checking and SMT, adaptable to any domain definable by SMT formulas, allowing for modular scalability and improved human understanding via metric-driven optimization. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through its application to configuring a CGRA memory tile for diverse image processing tasks.

This study examines the operator growth phenomenon in Lie-symmetric systems by utilizing concepts from quantum information theory. We specifically analyze Krylov complexity, entanglement properties, and information capacity within SU(1,1) and SU(2) symmetric systems, leveraging two-mode coherent states as a primary tool. These coherent states enable us to explore operator growth patterns and entanglement structures in a systematic manner, ultimately verifying that certain fundamental features emerge across these systems in alignment with the universal operator growth hypothesis. Moreover, our work showcases the value of leveraging Lie symmetry, which streamlines calculations and renders existing approaches like the Lanczos algorithm superfluous, instead allowing us to extract crucial insights through symmetry-based arguments.

Recently, WiFi has become the primary technique for locating individuals within indoor settings. This paper examines the use of WiFi data in positioning methods, focusing on two common data collection approaches. Experiments conducted in a medium-sized indoor office space demonstrate that two analyzed data types can achieve localization accuracy exceeding 2 meters. Notably, one approach, employing centered raw signal strength values from all access points, proved particularly effective in achieving this level of accuracy. As such, our research suggests that this approach may have a higher practical potential for deployment than currently anticipated.

For nearly 60 years, researchers have been searching for signs of extraterrestrial life through SETI initiatives, with a Dyson Sphere as a primary target - an advanced megastructure capable of harnessing a star's energy for an advanced civilization. A study explores whether constructing such a structure around a black hole would be feasible and efficient in powering a civilization, even though it wouldn't emit light like traditional Dyson Spheres. However, if this type of structure could control its host black hole's mass growth rate, it might make detection possible using astrometry and microlensing techniques. Furthermore, a rapid growth in stellar activity at galaxies containing Dyson Black Holes could serve as another indicator of their existence.

Network-based services are now commonly used, and generating income for service providers relies heavily on the agreements (SLAs) made with users. Since SLAs directly affect the financial stability of service providers, it's essential to determine feasible agreements that consider both the users' experiences and the financial aspect of the service. This paper proposes a novel approach to create an approachable framework for reaching agreements, considering the impact on users and financial stability. A specific model is used to refine this framework, which considers specific factors such as network performance, the impact on users, and revenue. It is shown that the problem can be solved efficiently and an effective solution strategy is presented to find practical agreements. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in terms of speed and reliability.

The beam breakup instability poses a challenge for particle accelerators and typically constrains the maximum beam current that can be achieved, especially for energy recovery linacs with multiple passes where a small amount of charge can generate a large beam current. Studies have highlighted the impact of filling patterns on beam performance in ERLinacs, particularly in structures with high shunt impedance per cell. This paper investigates filling pattern effects on beam performance in a specific energy recovery linacs structure, and demonstrates how certain filling patterns can lead to the onset of beam breakup instability at lower beam currents compared to the theoretical prediction using standard formulas. A new approach is developed to analyze beam breakup instability in energy recovery linacs by considering multiple passes and interaction between forward and backward propagating beam waves. This approach allows for a calculation of threshold beam currents for different filling patterns, and our results show that certain patterns can result in significantly lower threshold beam currents, particularly in structures with high shunt impedance per cell.

To determine the parameters for neutrino oscillation, cutting-edge experiments employing long-baseline neutrino detection systems rely heavily on the development of detailed models describing the interactions between neutrinos and atomic nuclei. These models must be exceptionally precise in order to be useful for analyzing results from experiments with deep-inelastic scattering events, involving the participation of multiple partons. We have carried out an in-depth analysis of neutrino-nucleus interactions, involving the scattering of a single parton, multiple parton scattering, final-state interactions, and nuclear effects such as final-state interactions and shadowing. As part of this comprehensive study, we have compiled full predictions, utilizing the Monte Carlo simulation tool FLUKA for scintillator tracker predictions, and have compared these predictions with full Monte Carlo simulations, taking into account all scattering processes modeled within FLUKA. Our comparative analysis revealed that, for high-energy neutrino interactions (above 10 GeV), the neutrino energy spectrum extracted from the hadron energy distribution, as measured by FLUKA, exhibits a bias of approximately 10%. This discrepancy arises due to a combination of factors, including the treatment of hadronization and energy deposition in the simulation, as well as the detection system's response. In a previous study, we investigated the sticking forces between particles with a chondritic composition and minimal sticking barriers, discovering a strong inverse relationship between sticking forces and temperatures above 100K. In this continued examination, we aimed to determine the role of surface moisture on the sticking barriers of these chondritic particles, examining them at multiple temperatures from 200K down to 50K. In contrast to our earlier investigation, we discovered no significant correlation between sticking forces and temperatures within this new, broader temperature scope. In the 200K - 100K temperature range, we observed the sticking forces decreasing as temperatures dropped, mirroring our previous findings. In the 100K - 50K range, we observed the stick probabilities of 50K particles to be notably lower than those of 50 nanometer diameter particles at other temperatures. In addition, we observed 50K particles to exhibit no temperature dependence in this range, showing similar behavior to 200K down to 100 nanometers diameter particles at other temperatures. In order to better understand this, we developed a theoretical model incorporating both thermal and cold water contributions to sticking forces of these particles. In order to address the loss of sticking barrier in 50K particles, we developed a model that posits a thin water film that forms on 50K particles and facilitates their nucleation of ice. Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis (LFDA) is a localized adaptation of the traditional Fisher Discriminant Analysis, widely employed for supervised dimensionality reduction techniques. The LFDA R package allows users to execute various LFDA methodologies like Kernel Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis and Semi-Supervised Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis. The package also facilitates dimensionality reduction result visualization, utilizing 3D (rgl) and 2D (ggfortify in ggplot2) graphical tools.

Imitation learning has emerged as a key approach for robot skill learning due to its user-friendly and straightforward solution for robot trajectory generation. Despite various movement primitive representations being utilized, most current approaches suffer from limited generalization when adapting to new target poses and fail to effectively combine common elements from multiple demonstrations. This research introduces Extended Kernelized Movement Primitives (EKMP), a novel representation that EKMP employs an extended kernel to adapt demonstration variability to robot adaptation EKMP's capability to adapt demonstration variability to robot adaptation EKMP's ability to adapt demonstration variability to robot adaptation. EKMP's advantage over existing kernel adaptation methods is its extended kernel's ability to adapt demonstration variability to robot adaptation. EKMP's ability to adapt demonstration variability to robot adaptation.

To extend the BFKL equation to NNLL accuracy, the one-loop CEV for two gluons with low rapidity ordering must be known. In this work, the dispersive part of a one-loop six-gluon amplitude in N=4 SYM theory was calculated under a NMRK kinematic limit. This calculation was performed in terms of six invariant cross ratios, and then, by applying an appropriate high energy limit to a specific six-gluon amplitude in the "heavily reggeized" regime, the relevant rapidity invariant was isolated, allowing extraction of the CEV for two gluons in its integral form. This procedure mirrors a previous method used to derive a simpler Regge limit from a specific six-gluon amplitude. Notably, the resulting CEV depends on three of the six instanton form factors constituting the six-gluon amplitude in N=4 SYM theory. Due to this connection, an additional property of the CEV is also investigated.

A novel class of superconductors featuring antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling and placed within a Zeeman magnetic field may be used to create fault-tolerant quantum computations via topologically non-Abelian states. Employing a Bose-Einstein condensation approach for electron pairs in the BCS limit, we derive the superconducting state's properties, taking into account Rashba spin-orbit coupling, Zeeman splitting, and the potential attraction between electrons. We demonstrate that the Rashba coupling and Zeeman field work in opposition, with the latter ultimately breaking the topologically protected superconducting state. Additionally, we show that our approach accounts for Rashba-induced band splitting and incorporate a potential solution to enhance the critical point defined by our method.

By utilizing sound wave velocity and absorption measurements in very strong magnetic fields, we have found a previously unobserved state transition in the interlocked vortex lattice structure of the doped material La$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$CuO$_4$. The discovery was made by examining the samples at various temperatures and with varying magnetic fields directed perpendicular to the copper-oxygen planes, using second sound interferometry in the flux-jamming state. Our results for x = 0.04, 0.05, and 0.10 indicate that at T < 25 K and at T < 40, 60 K respectively, the increasing La$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$CuO$_4$ experiences a closed-loop phase transition in response to high magnetic fields. The results also show that the two-state model is insufficient to explain the findings of three-component sound measurements under high magnetic fields in the pinned vortex glass state.

Theories describing weakly interacting polymer brushes have been expanded upon a curve-defined surface, a modification that reveals the significance of end exclusion zones in theoretical modeling. This expansion implies that end exclusion volumes vary in proportion to the $1/R$ factor, where $1/R$ represents the curvature of the substrate. This finding underscores the necessity of considering end exclusion zones in the theoretical analysis of polymer brushes on curved surfaces. Moreover, our model suggests that incorporating $1/R$ factors into the 'strong interaction limit' model may enhance its applicability to a broader context. A comparison with Molecular Dynamics simulations confirms that the modified 'weak interaction limit' model and the updated 'strong interaction limit' model both effectively characterize polymer brush behavior on curved surfaces.

A graph G is considered fully identifiable when a subset of its vertices R can pinpoint each vertex uniquely by determining their distance to every point in R. A sub-set of R that does this best with the fewest points is known as the minimum identifying set or "metric dimension" of the graph. Here we discuss the version of this property where the shortest distances between points are capped at some number k and call it beta_k of the graph.

Researchers explored a novel approach to enhance image quality using a space-based telescope by training a machine learning model on a dataset of distorted and improved images from the same source. When evaluated on a separate dataset of Hubble Space Telescope images, this method successfully demonstrated a significant improvement in the quality of astronomical images. Notably, it outperformed a conventional method known as 2x3 median stacking and showed comparable results to a more advanced technique called CRPSST, despite requiring less than half the computing time.

Inspired by the effectiveness of the serial dictatorship mechanism in resolving group decision-making challenges, we investigate its potential for solving a range of combinatorial optimization problems by employing a basic model where multiple agents take sequential actions. Specifically, we focus on unweighted maximum weight independent set and cluster editing problems, as well as their weighted counterparts, in which instance elements are assigned values by means of an allocation function. We find that certain combinatorial optimization problems exhibit exponential approximations even when the number of required rounds is limited to a small constant, while other problems can be solved with constant-factor guarantees; notably, we demonstrate an unweighted cluster editing approximation that is significantly superior to the previously established bound of 2 + $\epsilon$. Moreover, we explore a combinatorial optimization variant of the protocol popularized in economics and computer science literature by Balinski and Laraki's "Decision and Policy: The Science of Collective Choice", in which the set of available actions is governed by the serial dictatorship mechanism. We find that, for a range of problems, this variant yields outcomes comparable to the best possible solutions when the number of required rounds is limited to a small constant, while in some instances, it ensures outcomes that are substantially better than previously established bounds.

We have identified 19 unique wide binary asteroids from our dataset that could not be found by previous researchers using astrometric techniques. This finding is significant as it offers insight into the prevalence of marginally stable asteroid binaries, the limits of detection through astrometry, and the characteristics of binary systems with different durations. To achieve this, we utilized our existing dataset of approximately 400 tightly correlated objects to calculate the probability of detecting wide binary companions, which revealed a 25% increase in the overall binary ratio of main belt asteroids when adding these discoveries. This discovery process highlights the effectiveness of our method in detecting tight binaries and their potential to serve as precursors for identifying wide binary partners. As a result, our research presents a robust pipeline for systematically searching for bound binary systems of varying configurations.

This research supplements the findings related to the specified context, model, and estimation methods initially presented by Auerbach in 2019. The paper's first section explores the asymptotic behavior of the estimators presented in section 2 of the Auerbach's work. The second section investigates extensions to the model. The third section applies the model to estimate peer effects within networks. The fourth section presents results obtained from simulated data.

This study introduces novel versions of the Leibniz Rule for the Riemann-Liouville Variable-Order fractional integral and derivative. It derives key formulas, including product, quotient, and chain rules for both the integral and differential operators. Specifically, four distinct product rule formulas, four quotient rule formulas derived from product rule types, and four chain rule formulas have been established.

This paper analyzes the performance of complex MIMO systems that utilize spatial modulation and multiuser detection with a least-squares method, and derives rate and distortion metrics for this setup. By applying an asymptotic characterization, we evaluate specific detector methods, including an optimal Bayesian detector, and develop a simplified approach for optimizing a related detection method, before supporting our findings with numerical simulations.

We've developed an open-source suite of web visualization tools tailored for
analyzing spectral and imaging data, which are being utilized in the second edition
of the RCSDC galaxy energy distribution catalog (rcs2). These tools are particularly
effective in deriving various derived quantities from energy distributions spectra, such as
galaxy star formation rates, masses of bulges and black holes, as well as verifying
